newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean petrol price up 2 pct after deregulation.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean petrol price up 2 pct after deregulation.

text.p: Petrol prices at South Korean pumps rose an average of two percent after the government freed price controls on January 1, oil industry officials said on Friday.
The prices at filling stations rose to an average of 828-829 won per litre between Wednesday and Thursday from 815 won, they said.
"Prices are being set at similar levels because everyone is conforming to a uniform price level," said one official from a major oil company. "No one wants to be quotabuster."
Kerosene prices increased to 387-388 won a litre from 346 won and diesel prices rose to 382-385 won from 347 won.
From January 1, domestic prices of gasoline, kerosene, diesel and C-type fuel were deregulated and no longer subject to a government-set monthly price ceiling.
The new regime is part of a wider deregulation of oil product imports and exports, loosening the grip of refineries on the oil trade.
Until the end of June, oil refiners must give the government advance notice of price changes on gasoline, kerosene and diesel. After that, only notification after the fact is required.
But the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy said it would intervene if prices became too volatile and endangered the stability of the economy.
Refiners found guilty of price fixing or setting prices artificially low to grab market share would be punished according to the Fair Trade Act.
